function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Quick Reference** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (75 mph on some interstates).
• In cities: 25–45 mph (often 35 mph).
• Rural roads: 55 mph unless posted otherwise. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 years or 4 ft 9 in tall must use a child safety seat. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• For commercial drivers: BAC ≥ 0.04 %.
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, possible jail time. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has priority.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | | **School‑Bus Rules** | • Stop for all vehicles when a school bus stops and signals.
• Cannot pass a stopped school bus. | | **Headlights & Taillights** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Taillights must be on at all times. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• No passing on the right unless the left lane is occupied or the vehicle is turning left. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | | **Traffic Signal Violations** | • Running red lights, stop signs, or yielding to pedestrians is a moving‑violation offense. | | **Vehicle Registration & Insurance** | • Registration must be renewed annually.
• Proof of insurance is required; minimum liability coverage applies. | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Vehicles may be towed for violations such as illegal parking or being a hazard. | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Motorcycles: helmet required for riders under 18 or with a license under 18.
• Commercial vehicles: must follow specific weight and safety regulations. | **Where to Find Official Texts** - Texas Transportation Code (Title 7, Chapter 1) – the statutory source for all traffic laws. - Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) – provides handbooks, driver’s manuals, and enforcement guidelines. - Texas Legislature Online – searchable database of statutes and legislative history. **Common Enforcement Practices** - **Traffic Stops**: Officers may issue citations for speeding, seat‑belt violations, or DUI. - **Traffic School**: First‑time offenders may attend a state‑approved traffic school to avoid points on their license. - **Points System**: Accumulating 4 points in 12 months can lead to license suspension. **Resources for Further Information** - **Texas DPS Driver Handbook** – downloadable PDF. - **Texas DOT Traffic Safety Reports** – annual statistics on accidents and enforcement. - **Legal Aid & Law Firms** – for representation if facing a traffic ticket or DUI charge. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law, how to contest a ticket, or how to register a vehicle in Texas!
